A0265.title: Ticket Resale Control
A0265.definition: Reduce ticket scalping by binding tickets to verified identities, checking transfer eligibility, limiting transfer frequency, and keeping transfers inside official channels.
A0265.description:
Ticket resale control applies to scarce-resource allocation scenarios such as concerts, sports events, attraction reservations, medical appointments, transport seats, and activity slots. It places real-name binding, transferor and transferee identity checks, transfer-count limits, markup limits, official transfer channels, and abnormal-transfer freezes around purchase, issuance, transfer, refund, entry, and redemption workflows.

The core of this control is to keep ownership transfer inside a platform-managed loop, reducing scalper profit through transfer codes, account delivery, offline deals, or marked-up secondary-platform resale. Implementation should distinguish legitimate friend or family transfers, refund circulation, and professional scalping based on ticket type, event risk level, regulatory requirements, consumer refund needs, and entry-verification capability.
A0265.limitation: Overly strict transfer limits can harm legitimate refund, exchange, and friend-or-family purchase needs, creating complaints and compliance disputes. Scalpers may still bypass in-platform controls through whole-account delivery, accompanied entry, forged identity materials, off-site cash transactions, or inducing users to share accounts. This control should be combined with real-name verification, device risk control, secondary-platform monitoring, and complaint handling.
